items.review_rationale: Reviewed local uniform convergence of functions to a metric target with one neighborhood per domain point and uniform convergence of restrictions on that neighborhood.

references.context: For each x∈X select an open or neighborhood subset U_x containing x; no single U works for every x.
Functions f_n|U_x and f|U_x compared uniformly on the chosen neighborhood.

references.disposition: Quantifiers permit a different neighborhood and convergence threshold across domain points.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed pointwise convergence of real functions using epsilon and point-dependent index threshold, retaining domain and fixed point quantification.

references.context: Natural index may depend on evaluation point x and tolerance epsilon.

references.phrase: for all n≥N and fixed x
references.disposition: Threshold cannot be required uniformly in x; that would impose a stronger condition.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed pointwise convergence of functions to topological codomain through convergence as a sequence in function product space T^D with product topology.

references.context: Product of a copy of T for each domain input d∈D, identified with all functions D→T.
For each basic product-topology neighborhood of limit function, eventually all sequence functions belong to it.

references.disposition: In product topology, only finitely many coordinates are restricted by each basic open neighborhood.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed uniform convergence into metric space with one epsilon-dependent threshold valid across all domain points, unlike pointwise convergence.

references.context: For every positive tolerance epsilon there exists one natural index bound independent of x∈S.
After threshold, inequality applies simultaneously to all domain inputs x.

references.disposition: All domain points are quantified after the existence of a single N for each epsilon.
